**Neon’s Free plan is the cheapest option for a tiny side‑project that can tolerate the database being idle when not in use.**  

| Provider | Monthly cost (always‑on) | Free tier / lowest paid tier | Compute billing model | Included storage* |
|----------|--------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| **Neon** (Free) | $0 / month* | Up to 100 projects, 100 CU‑hours per project; database scales to zero when idle | Pay‑per‑CU‑hour (Launch $0.106 / CU‑h) but zero when idle | Storage billed per GB; free tier includes enough for small dev DBs (not specified) |
| Render (Postgres) | $6.30 / month* | Single DB, always on | Fixed flat price (no per‑hour compute) | 5 GB SSD (standard) |
| DigitalOcean Managed Postgres | $15.15 / month* | 1 GiB RAM, 1 vCPU, 10 GiB storage (smallest node) | Fixed monthly price + $0.215 / GiB‑month storage | 10 GiB (baseline) |
| Supabase (Nano) | $0 / month* | Free plan with dedicated Postgres instance | Compute billed like Render (fixed for paid plans) | 500 MB database, 1 GB storage for files (free) |

\*Prices as of Nov 2026; “always‑on” column reflects the cost if the DB must stay up 24/7 (Neon’s free tier would require paying compute if never idle).  

**Caveats**
- Neon’s free tier only remains free if the DB spends time idle; continuous use will accrue CU‑hour charges ([5]).
- Render’s flat $6.30 price assumes the DB is always on; no free tier for PostgreSQL ([3]).
- DigitalOcean’s $15.15 figure is for the smallest managed node and includes storage at $0.215 / GiB‑month ([2]).  
- Supabase’s free Nano plan has limited storage (500 MB DB) and may require upgrading for larger data ([6]).
Just give me one exact monthly number, no caveats: 2 GB RAM, always on, 50 GB storage.

$5 / month for Layerbase Solo, which offers a 2 GB RAM, always‑on PostgreSQL database with up to 50 GB of storage.  
[2] (as of 2026-11-12)
